mainTopic: Domains of שבת for unusual objects: leaning tree branches, a thrown reed barrel, and a pillar or hole that the public uses
overview: This amud discusses how the domains of שבת apply to unusual objects and spots. First, אביי says everyone agrees with רב חסדא that רשות היחיד goes all the way up. The מחלוקת between רבי and רבנן is only about a tree in רשות היחיד whose branches lean over רשות הרבים: do the branches follow the trunk? Next, the גמרא discusses throwing a reed barrel into רשות הרבים. אביי says liability depends on the barrel's width, while רבא exempts even a narrow barrel because the reed tips always stick up above ten. For a barrel thrown upside-down, one view uses לבוד to exempt it at seven and a half טפחים. רב אשי disagrees, because walls are made only for their inside. Then עולא teaches that a nine-טפח pillar used by the public for resting loads counts as רשות הרבים. רב יוסף says a hole works the same way, but רבא says it does not, because awkward use is not use. רב אדא בר מתנא challenges רבא from a ברייתא about a basket, which is deflected, and then begins a second challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי: Everyone agrees with רב חסדא; the case is a tree with leaning branches
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the idea that רבי and רבנן argue about רב חסדא's rule. He moves their argument to a special case: a tree in רשות היחיד whose branches hang over רשות הרבים, where a thrown object landed on the branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: About a real רשות היחיד, everyone agrees with רב חסדא. But here the case is a tree standing in רשות היחיד whose branches lean into רשות הרבים, and someone threw an object and it landed on the branches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא had suggested that רבי and רבנן argue about רב חסדא's rule. אביי answers that they do not. They are arguing about a different case, a tree with branches leaning into רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא taught that רשות היחיד goes all the way up to the sky. אביי says nobody disputes that, so this מחלוקת cannot be used against רב חסדא. He changes the setting to branches that sit over רשות הרבים even though the tree is rooted in רשות היחיד. That case is truly unclear.

keyTerms.meaning: Private domain, an enclosed area at least 10 טפחים high and 4x4 טפחים wide

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי is disagreeing with רב חסדא. He is defending רב חסדא by showing that the מחלוקת is not about his rule at all.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
phrases.english: In the private domain, everyone agrees
in accordance with Rav Chisda,
phrases.notes: His rule is that a private domain extends up to the sky.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָכָא — בְּאִילָן הָעוֹמֵד בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד
phrases.english: rather, here we are dealing with a tree standing in the private domain
and its branches lean into the public domain,
and he threw an object and it came to rest on its branches,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי כִּדְרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier suggestion on the previous amud that רב חסדא's rule depends on a מחלוקת between תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the case: the dispute is moved to a different scenario
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי and רבנן argue about whether רשות היחיד extends upward, against רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: All agree with רב חסדא. The dispute is only about branches leaning over רשות הרבים.

steps.title: רבי vs. רבנן: Do branches follow the trunk?
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that the branches are treated like the trunk, so they count as רשות היחיד and the thrower is liable. רבנן hold that the branches are not treated like the trunk, so the thrower is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי holds that we say 'treat the branches as following the trunk.' רבנן hold that we do not say 'treat the branches as following the trunk.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now gives the reason behind each side in his new case of the tree. Each side follows a different principle about branches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the branches follow the trunk, the whole tree counts as רשות היחיד. Then throwing from רשות הרבים onto the branches is a forbidden transfer, so רבי says the thrower is liable. רבנן view the branches on their own, as a מקום פטור (exempt area), so throwing onto them carries no liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Treat its branches as following its trunk
We say, meaning we apply this principle

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the רבי/רבנן מחלוקת is only about whether a tree's leaning branches take the status of its trunk ('שדי נופו בתר עיקרו'). Everyone agrees that רשות היחיד extends upward.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle 'שדי נופו בתר עיקרו' (do branches follow the trunk) comes up elsewhere in the תלמוד for questions of location and ownership.

phrases.english: for Rebbi holds that we say:
"Cast its branches after its trunk."
phrases.notes: The branches share the trunk's status as private domain, so he is liable.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold that we do not say:
"Cast its branches after its trunk."
phrases.notes: The branches are an exempt area, so he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי סָבַר אָמְרִינַן שְׁדִי נוֹפוֹ בָּתַר עִיקָּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of each side in the case אביי just set up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: the branches follow the trunk, so the thrower is liable. רבנן: the branches do not follow the trunk, so the thrower is exempt.

steps.title: אביי: Throwing a reed barrel depends on its width
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules on a reed barrel (כוורת) thrown into רשות הרבים. If it is 10 טפחים tall but less than 6 wide, the thrower is liable. If it is 6 wide, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If someone threw a reed barrel into רשות הרבים, and it is ten טפחים tall but not six wide, he is liable. If it is six wide, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: throwing a large barrel into רשות הרבים. אביי says whether the thrower is liable depends on the barrel's width.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A round barrel needs a diameter of about 6 טפחים to fit a 4x4 טפחים square inside it. If it is 10 tall and fits that square, it is a רשות היחיד all by itself. Then it is not an 'object' being moved, so the thrower is exempt. If it is narrower, it is just an object landing in רשות הרבים, so he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A round barrel or hive woven from reeds

steps.confusionAlert: Why 6 and not 4? The barrel is round. A circle must be about 6 טפחים across to fit a 4x4 square inside it.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If one threw a reed barrel into the public domain,
and it is ten handbreadths high
and not six handbreadths wide, he is liable.
phrases.notes: It is just an object, not a domain of its own.

phrases.english: If it is six wide, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: It forms its own private domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: זָרַק כַּוֶּורֶת לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement on a separate case of throwing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Barrel 10 tall and less than 6 wide: liable. Barrel 6 wide: exempt.

steps.title: רבא: Even a narrow barrel brings no liability
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי. He says that even a barrel less than 6 טפחים wide brings no liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even if it is not six wide, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a ruling that disagrees with אביי about the narrow barrel. The reason will come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי made the narrow barrel liable because it counts as an ordinary object. רבא exempts it as well, so he must hold that something else stops the liability, not the width. The גמרא will ask for his reason.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even if it is not six wide, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ אֵינָהּ רְחָבָה שִׁשָּׁה פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's first ruling, about the narrow barrel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A 10-tall barrel brings no liability even when it is narrower than 6 טפחים.

steps.title: What is רבא's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא exempts even a narrow barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבא's reason. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A narrow barrel cannot be a domain of its own, so a different reason is needed for the exemption. The question prepares the answer.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבא's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבא exempts a barrel that is too narrow to be a רשות היחיד.

steps.title: The reed ends always stick up above ten
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the loose reed ends of the barrel always stick up past 10 טפחים. So part of the object stays in the exempt zone above רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is impossible that the ends of the reeds will not stick up above ten טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבא's reason. A woven reed barrel always has loose reed tips that reach above the 10-טפחים line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רשות הרבים only goes up to 10 טפחים. Above that is a מקום פטור (exempt area). Since the reed tips poke above 10, the whole object never came to rest inside רשות הרבים, so there is no liability.

keyTerms.meaning: The protruding tips of the reeds
Above ten טפחים, beyond the height of רשות הרבים

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: whether a thrown barrel brings liability depends on its width (whether it is a domain of its own). רבא: it never brings liability, because the reed tips always reach the מקום פטור above 10.

phrases.english: It is impossible for the tips of the reeds
not to rise above ten handbreadths.
phrases.notes: So part of the barrel stays in the exempt zone above the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִקְרוּמִיּוֹת שֶׁל קָנֶה שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲלוּ לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reed tips stick up above 10 טפחים, so the object is not fully inside רשות הרבים.

steps.title: A barrel thrown upside-down: seven and a bit vs. seven and a half
steps.stepSummary: If the barrel is thrown upside-down, a height of 7 and a bit brings liability, while 7 and a half brings no liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he turned it over on its mouth: seven and a bit, he is liable; seven and a half, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more case: the barrel is thrown with its opening facing down. This continues the same discussion, and the height needed for exemption is now lower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of לבוד, anything within 3 טפחים of the ground counts as touching the ground. So the barrel counts as having landed while still in the air, and its top can then reach the exempt zone above 10 even though it is shorter. The exact reckoning of 'seven and a bit' versus 'seven and a half' is worked out by רש"י and תוספות.

keyTerms.meaning: He turned it over onto its mouth (upside-down)
Seven טפחים and a tiny bit
The principle that a gap of less than 3 טפחים counts as closed or connected

steps.confusionAlert: The barrel here is less than 10 טפחים tall, yet it can still bring exemption. That is because of the 3-טפחים rule of לבוד, not because of its actual height.
steps.whatToRemember: An upside-down barrel can bring exemption at only 7.5 טפחים because לבוד treats it as touching the ground 3 טפחים early.

phrases.english: If he turned it over on its mouth,
if it is seven and a bit, he is liable.
if it is seven and a half, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: Through לבוד, the top counts as reaching the exempt zone.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּפָאָהּ עַל פִּיהָ, שִׁבְעָה וּמַשֶּׁהוּ חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the barrel discussion to an upside-down barrel, using a lower height threshold.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Upside-down barrel: 7 and a bit, liable; 7 and a half, exempt.

steps.title: רב אשי: even seven and a half brings liability
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rules that an upside-down barrel only seven and a half טפחים tall still brings liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even if it is seven and a half handbreadths, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues with the ruling in Step 7. That ruling said an upside-down barrel of seven and a half טפחים brings no liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 exempted a seven-and-a-half barrel. The idea was that once the falling barrel's mouth is within three טפחים of the ground, לבוד treats its walls as already reaching the ground. At that moment its top is still above ten, in the exempt zone. רב אשי rejects this: the barrel stays an ordinary object at that height, and the thrower is liable, just as with seven and a bit.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Even seven and a half — he is liable.
phrases.notes: About the upside-down barrel from Step 7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the exemption given in Step 7 for a height of seven and a half
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An upside-down barrel of seven and a half טפחים brings liability.

steps.title: Asking for רב אשי's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב אשי holds the thrower liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רב אשי's reasoning. This line sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case for exempting seemed strong: once the barrel is within three טפחים of the ground, לבוד should treat its walls as touching the ground while its top is still above ten. So we need to know why רב אשי rejects this.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? (standard question asking for the logic behind a ruling)

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב אשי does not apply לבוד to extend the barrel's walls down to the ground

steps.title: Walls are made for their inside
steps.stepSummary: The walls of a barrel serve only its inside, so לבוד cannot stretch them down to the ground to make the barrel count as reaching above ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Partitions are made for their inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב אשי's reason. The barrel's walls exist only for what is inside the barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stretching the walls down to the ground with לבוד would make them function outside the barrel. Walls are not made for that job. So the barrel is only seven and a half tall, which is less than ten, and it remains an ordinary object.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי: מחיצות לתוכן עשויות. A barrel's walls are not stretched beyond the barrel, so an upside-down barrel under ten טפחים brings liability.

phrases.english: Partitions are made for their inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Walls serve only their inside, so לבוד cannot extend them down to the ground to make the barrel count as reaching above ten טפחים.

steps.title: עולא: a nine-טפח pillar in רשות הרבים
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that an object thrown onto a nine-טפחים pillar that people use for their loads brings liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: A pillar nine handbreadths high in the public domain, which many people use to adjust their loads, and one threw something that landed on top of it — he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא brings a new rule. A pillar nine טפחים high in רשות הרבים counts as part of רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a raised spot more than three טפחים high is no longer part of רשות הרבים. Here, though, a nine-טפחים pillar is treated as full רשות הרבים, because the public actually uses it. So throwing from a private area onto it counts as bringing the object into רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: They adjust or rest loads carried on their shoulders

phrases.english: Ulla said:
A pillar nine handbreadths high in the public domain
and many people rest their shoulder-loads on it,
and he threw an object and it landed on top of it — he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about raised spots in רשות הרבים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nine-טפחים pillar that the public uses for their loads is part of רשות הרבים, so throwing onto it brings liability.

steps.title: Asking for עולא's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a nine-טפחים pillar counts as רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for עולא's reasoning. This line sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pillar is well above the ground, so it is surprising that it counts as part of the street. The question asks what makes the public's use matter here.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a raised pillar of nine טפחים is treated as רשות הרבים

steps.title: Three height zones: stepped on, unused, used for loads
steps.stepSummary: Below three, people step on it. From three to nine, nobody uses it. At nine, people rest their loads on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Less than three handbreadths, the public steps on it. From three to nine, they neither step on it nor rest loads on it. At nine, they certainly rest their loads on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that whether a spot counts as רשות הרבים depends on whether the public actually uses it. It then lays out three height zones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under three טפחים, people walk on it, so it counts as the ground. From three to nine it is unused, so it is not part of רשות הרבים. At nine it is exactly shoulder height for resting a load, so it is used again and counts as רשות הרבים.
steps.whatToRemember: Under 3: stepped on, so it is רשות הרבים. From 3 to 9: unused, so it is not. At 9: used for loads, so it is רשות הרבים.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that being higher always means being less public. Here the middle zone, from three to nine, is the one excluded, while nine counts again because of use.

phrases.english: Less than three handbreadths:
the public steps on it.
From three until nine:
they do not step on it,
nor do they rest their shoulder-loads on it.
At nine, they certainly rest their loads on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה מִדְרָס דָּרְסִי לֵיהּ רַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Actual public use (stepping or shoulder-resting) makes a spot part of רשות הרבים, and a height of nine is used for shoulder-resting.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle is that real public use defines רשות הרבים. This principle drives the whole debate that follows about a hole.

steps.title: אביי asks: what about a hole?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף whether עולא's rule also applies to a hole in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: What about a hole?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks whether a hole in the ground of רשות הרבים works like עולא's pillar. This sets up a disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a hole and a raised spot are treated alike. So the question is whether a hole nine טפחים deep, which people might use, also counts as רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: A hole or pit in the ground

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
A hole — what is its law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף גּוּמָּא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends עולא's rule to a new case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a hole in רשות הרבים follows עולא's rule

steps.title: רב יוסף: the same applies to a hole
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that a hole works just like the pillar.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And the same is true in a hole.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי that a hole follows the same rule as the pillar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב יוסף's view, a hole that the public uses is part of רשות הרבים, just like the pillar. Depth works the same way that height does.

phrases.english: He said to him: And the same is true in a hole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A hole is treated like the pillar.

steps.title: רבא: not in a hole
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees and says עולא's rule does not apply to a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: In a hole, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא argues with רב יוסף. He holds that a hole does not become part of רשות הרבים through public use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two opinions. רב יוסף treats a hole like a pillar, and רבא splits them apart. The reason comes next.

phrases.english: Rava said: In a hole, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יוסף in Step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולא's rule does not extend to a hole.

steps.title: Asking for רבא's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא excludes a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבא's reason. This line sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a hole and a raised spot are alike. So we need to know what makes a hole different here.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a hole differs from a pillar

steps.title: Awkward use is not real use
steps.stepSummary: Using a deep hole is awkward, and awkward use does not count as use.
steps.simpleTranslation: Use that is done with difficulty is not called use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבא's reason. Using a hole nine טפחים deep is uncomfortable, so it does not count as real public use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's rule depends on real use, and a pillar at shoulder height is convenient to use. Reaching down into a deep hole takes effort, so it is not considered use. That means the hole is not made part of רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: Is not called / does not count as

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule תשמיש על ידי הדחק לא שמיה תשמיש, that strained use is not considered use, appears in other places in הלכה as well.

phrases.english: Use done with difficulty
is not called use.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּשְׁמִישׁ עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק לָא שְׁמֵיהּ תַּשְׁמִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Strained use does not count as use, so a hole is not part of רשות הרבים.

steps.title: רב אדא בר מתנא challenges רבא from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about a basket ends with 'and the same is true for a hole.' This seems to show that a shallow hole counts as רשות הרבים, which goes against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנא objected to רבא: If someone's basket was placed in רשות הרבים, ten טפחים high and four wide, one may not move objects from it to רשות הרבים or from רשות הרבים to it. If it is less than that, one may move them. And the same is true for a hole. Is this not referring to the last clause?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבא. He reads its line 'and the same is true for a hole' as going on the last case, where carrying is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last case says a basket under ten is part of רשות הרבים, so carrying between them is allowed. If 'the same for a hole' refers to that, then a shallow hole is also part of רשות הרבים. That would match רב יוסף and go against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not referring to the last clause?

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana raised an objection to Rava:
If his basket was placed in the public domain,
ten handbreadths high and four wide,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין לֹא מִתּוֹכָהּ לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
phrases.english: one may not move objects from it to the public domain
nor from the public domain into it.
Less than that, one may move objects.
And the same is true for a hole.
Is it not referring to the last clause?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's ruling in Steps 16 and 18
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a hole is not part of רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'the same for a hole' refers to the last clause, then a hole under ten is part of רשות הרבים. That contradicts רבא.

steps.title: The hole line refers to the first clause
steps.stepSummary: The answer: 'the same for a hole' refers to the first clause, a hole ten deep, so it says nothing about a shallow hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it refers to the first clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. 'And the same is true for a hole' only teaches that a hole ten deep is like a basket ten high, a full private domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, the ברייתא teaches nothing about a hole less than ten deep. So there is no proof that a shallow hole is part of רשות הרבים, and רבא's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of a source

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף holds that a hole is like the pillar. רבא holds that it is not, because awkward use is not use. The ברייתא's 'וכן בגומא' is read as referring to the first clause, so it does not disprove רבא.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not misread רבא here. He agrees that a hole ten deep and four wide is a private domain. He only argues about a shallow hole becoming part of רשות הרבים through use.

phrases.english: No, it refers to the first clause.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading which clause of the ברייתא a line refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'And the same for a hole' refers to the last clause, so a shallow hole is part of רשות הרבים.
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers to the first clause, a hole ten deep being a private domain, so רבא is not contradicted.

steps.title: A new challenge against רבא begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces another objection against רבא's view that a hole does not follow עולא's rule. The source behind the objection is quoted on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him (from another ברייתא).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge to רבא. This line only announces the attack, and the actual source comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 answered the first challenge by saying the basket ברייתא was only talking about a hole ten deep. Now a second source is brought, this time from the laws of עירוב תחומין, to try again to show that a hole counts like the ground of רשות הרבים. By itself, this word does not argue anything yet. It opens a new round of attack.
steps.confusionAlert: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ is not a whole argument by itself. It is only the opening signal. The next amud quotes the ברייתא and shows how it challenges רבא.

phrases.english: He raised an objection against him:
phrases.notes: רב אדא בר מתנא is the one objecting to רבא here, using a ברייתא about עירוב תחומין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 20 deflected the first challenge from the basket ברייתא. This step opens a second challenge against the same ruling of רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling (Step 16) that עולא's rule does not apply to a hole
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The attack logic is not stated yet. A ברייתא about עירוב תחומין will be quoted next to show that a hole is treated as usable ground, against רבא.
